title: PHARM · Blood transfusion reaction (STOP THE BLOOD, KEEP THE VEIN) (high stakes, night shift, Smart Prep errors)
hook: Nurses: 10 minutes into blood, her back hurts. Slow it?
hook_backups: Nurses: chills during a transfusion. Just slow it down?
Nurses: blood running, fever 38.6. Call first or stop first?
belief: A reaction during a transfusion means you slow the blood and call.

story.patient: 76-year-old woman with a stomach bleed, hemoglobin 6.8 g/dL, getting her first unit of packed red blood cells

timeline.beat: First unit of blood starts. Patient and nurse in frame with the hook
'Can you do her 15-minute vitals?' The nurse leaves the aide with her
timeline.mistake_line: Left the first 15 minutes to the aide

timeline.beat: 'My back hurts. I'm so cold.' Chills, temp 38.6 °C (101.5 °F), heart rate 118. The nurse slows the blood
timeline.mistake_line: Slowed the blood instead of stopping it

timeline.beat: Pages the provider and waits for a call back. The blood is still running
timeline.mistake_line: Called first, stopped the blood later

timeline.beat: BP (blood pressure) 78/44, dark red urine, oozing at the IV (intravenous) site
timeline.outcome: A transfusion reaction, worse with every minute the blood ran. 3 mistakes. Every one avoidable.

caught_it.text: Two-person check at the bedside: two identifiers, the unit, the order
The RN stays with her for the first 15 minutes, vitals per policy
Back pain, chills, fever: STOP the blood now
Keep the vein open: normal saline with new tubing. Stay, vitals, call the provider and blood bank

choice.question: Blood running. Back pain, chills, fever.
choice.a: Slow it down, call the provider
choice.b: Stop it, saline with new tubing, call

save_card.title: TRANSFUSION REACTION (STOP THE BLOOD, KEEP THE VEIN)

memory_line: Reaction? Stop the blood, keep the vein.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 1:10 AM. She's 76, a stomach bleed, hemoglobin 6.8. Her first unit of blood starts.

❌ 3 mistakes, 3 error types
1️⃣ Scope error: left the first 15 minutes to the aide
2️⃣ Habit over standard: back pain and chills, so the nurse slowed the blood
3️⃣ Wrong priority: paged the provider and waited, blood still running
➡️ 1:45 AM: BP (blood pressure) 78/44, dark red urine. Rapid response.

🩸 Transfusion reaction (STOP THE BLOOD, KEEP THE VEIN)
• Watch closely in the first 15 minutes: the most dangerous reactions often start early
• Signs: back pain, chills, fever, fast heart rate, low BP, dark urine, trouble breathing, hives

✅ The right move
• Two-person check at the bedside before it starts
• The RN (registered nurse) stays for the first 15 minutes, vitals per policy
• Any reaction sign: stop the blood first
• Keep the vein open with normal saline and new tubing
• Stay, vitals, call the provider and the blood bank. Send the bag and tubing back, per policy

🧠 Reaction? Stop the blood, keep the vein.
share_line: 📤 Send this to the nurse who'd slow the blood and wait for a call back.
sources: AABB (Association for the Advancement of Blood and Biotherapies) Technical Manual, current edition: recognizing and managing transfusion reactions
Lewis's Medical-Surgical Nursing, 13th ed. (2026): blood transfusion and acute transfusion reactions
rn_checks: Signs: back pain, chills, fever, tachycardia, hypotension, dark urine (hemoglobinuria), oozing at the IV site suggest an acute hemolytic reaction; the cause (usually a mismatch) is not shown. OK?
Stop the transfusion first; keep the vein open with normal saline through NEW tubing (not the blood set); stay, vitals, notify the provider and blood bank; return the bag and tubing per policy
RN stays with the patient and assesses during the first 15 minutes (common policy wording, 'per policy' on screen)
Two-person bedside check: two identifiers, the unit, the order
Story numbers: temp 38.6 °C, heart rate 118, then BP 78/44 over about 35 minutes. Realistic?
Lane: blood is a biologic, keyword PHARM. OK?
Memory phrase is NEW: (STOP THE BLOOD, KEEP THE VEIN). Keep or swap?
Smart Prep labels on the stamps: SCOPE ERROR, HABIT OVER STANDARD, WRONG PRIORITY. Fit?
Choice answer B; hook, cover and caption line 1 open with 'Nurses:'
smart_prep_note: Smart Prep error label (Cass, Nov 23): every MISTAKE stamp shows the error's simple name after the number, e.g. 'MISTAKE 1 · SCOPE ERROR', with the beat line under it. Every CAUGHT IT can carry a small anchor chip with the framework (e.g. 'ABC'). No product names, no pitch.
